lesson_blocks.body: What is AI? — plain words
AI predicts the next step from examples. You describe, it drafts; you check.
https://cdn.aimasterplan.app/intro/what-is-ai.mp4
lesson_blocks.caption: Watch: AI in 5 minutes

lesson_blocks.body: console.log('Hello, AI builder');

node --version
npm --version

GOAL: explain AI simply
CONTEXT: total beginner
CONSTRAINTS: no jargon
EXAMPLE: like explaining to a friend

Lesson: What is an LLM?

Add content using the lesson editor.
Vibe Coding: you direct, the AI types

Vibe Coding means describing what you want in plain words and letting an AI coding agent write the code.

Your job: describe clearly, run it, check the result, ask for fixes.
The agent's job: type, remember syntax, repeat forever without getting tired.

GOAL: get the agent to build [one small thing]
CONTEXT: I have never coded; my files are [list them]
CONSTRAINTS: change as little as possible, explain each step
EXAMPLE: 'Add a welcome message at the top of the page'

Lesson: AI vs Traditional Programming

Add content using the lesson editor.
Good prompts have 4 parts

GOAL: what done looks like.
CONTEXT: your files, errors, what you tried.
CONSTRAINTS: limits (small change, no new tools).
EXAMPLE: paste what 'done' looks like.

Weak: 'fix it'. Strong: GOAL + CONTEXT + CONSTRAINTS + EXAMPLE.

GOAL: [one sentence]
CONTEXT: [file + what you did + exact error]
CONSTRAINTS: [smallest change, explain why]
EXAMPLE OF DONE: [paste]

Lesson: Understanding Context

Add content using the lesson editor.
Files live in folders; names are addresses

A project is a folder of files.

- index.html = the page.
- styles.css = how it looks.
- app.js = what it does.
- server.js = the kitchen.
- data/ = the pantry.

The full name from the project root (like public/app.js) is the file's address. Share it when asking for help.

ls
ls public

Lesson: Basic Developer Terminology

Add content using the lesson editor.
Apps have 3 parts: what you see, the kitchen, the pantry

Every app has the same skeleton.

1. Frontend = what you see (buttons, text, pictures).
2. Backend = the kitchen (does the work when you tap).
3. Database = the pantry (remembers things).

They talk over a network: your tap travels frontend → backend → pantry and back.

GOAL: explain my app idea in 3 parts
CONTEXT: total beginner, my idea is [describe it]
CONSTRAINTS: plain words, no jargon
EXAMPLE: 'Frontend shows a list, backend saves it, database remembers it'

Lesson: Understand Client/Server Communication

Add content using the lesson editor.
APIs are menus for software

An API is a menu: you order (request) and get a dish (JSON response).

GET /api/tools = 'show me tools'. POST with JSON = 'take this order'.
Keys stay on the server (in .env), never in the page. Open the browser Network tab to watch orders go out.

GOAL: call [API name] and show [what]
CONTEXT: my code is [paste], the docs say [paste]
CONSTRAINTS: keep my key server-side
EXAMPLE: 'fetch the list and print the first item'

Databases remember rows

A database is a pantry of tables. Each table holds rows (like spreadsheet rows).

You do 5 things: create, read, update, delete, query (find).
CRUD = the first four. Start by reading one row before writing any.

// read all students (admin)
const r = await fetch('/api/cms/students', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + token } });

Authentication = who are you? Authorization = may you?

Sign-in proves identity (email + password → session token).
The token rides in the Authorization header on every private request.
Roles (student/instructor/author/admin) decide what each token may touch.
Passwords are salted hashes — the server never stores the real one.

AI APIs: your server asks the model, the page never holds the key

The page sends your words to YOUR server. Your server adds the secret key and asks the AI model. The answer comes back through your server.

Keys live in server .env only. Set spending caps. Stream long answers so the page feels alive.

CONTEXT: my server file is [paste], key is in .env
CONSTRAINTS: key never in client code, cap length
EXAMPLE: 'user asks X, assistant answers in 2 sentences'

Frontend + mobile: same API, two faces (web + Expo phone app)

Your backend API serves BOTH faces.

- Web face: HTML/CSS/JS pages.
- Mobile face: Expo (runs on iOS + Android from one codebase). Screens call the SAME /api endpoints with the user's token.

Build web first, then add 3 Expo screens (list, detail, profile) + auth + push. Ship phones via EAS → TestFlight/Play internal.

npx create-expo-app my-app
cd my-app
npx expo start

MVP: smallest thing that proves it + demo day

Cut everything except the ONE workflow that proves value.
Slice: auth → core CRUD → one AI step → test → deploy → 3-minute demo (problem, live click-through, what's next).
Ship, watch real users, improve weekly.

CONTEXT: my PRD is [paste]

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.what: Conversational AI for explanations and draft prompts.
tools.why: Ask anything in plain words and get explanations, examples and starter prompts.
tools.install: Create a free account at chat.openai.com — runs in the browser, nothing to install.
steps: Open chat.openai.com and sign up with email, Google or Apple.
Paste a lesson prompt, press Enter, read the answer fully.
Compare the answer against the lesson objective before moving on.

tools.name: AI Coding Assistant
tools.what: Writes and edits code from plain-word prompts.
tools.why: The core Vibe Coding engine: you describe, it writes the code, you review.
tools.install: Install an AI coding extension inside VS Code, then sign in.
steps: Open VS Code → Extensions → install an AI coding assistant.
Sign in and open the lesson project folder.
Paste the lesson prompt and review every file it creates.

tools.name: VS Code
tools.what: Free code editor with AI extensions.
tools.why: The home base where every project in this course gets built.
tools.install: Download the installer from code.visualstudio.com and accept the defaults.
steps: Download the installer for your OS and accept the defaults.
Open the lesson project folder (not a single file).
Open the built-in terminal with View → Terminal.

tools.name: Figma
tools.what: Free design tool for page mockups and layouts.
tools.why: Sketch screens before coding so you rebuild less and finish faster.
tools.install: Create a free account at figma.com — it runs in the browser.
steps: Sign up at figma.com on the free starter plan.
Make a phone-size frame (375×812) and block out 3 sections.
Share the link with your AI assistant as the design reference.

tools.name: Supabase
tools.what: Postgres + auth + storage with instant APIs.
tools.why: The backend for multi-user and AI apps: database, logins and file storage.
tools.install: Create a free project at supabase.com, then copy the URL + anon key into .env.
steps: Create a free project at supabase.com and wait for provisioning.
Table Editor → New table (e.g. leads) with the lesson fields.
Copy the Project URL + anon key into .env — never commit the service key.

tools.name: n8n
tools.what: Visual workflow builder: triggers → AI → actions.
tools.why: Run Level 7 automations without writing servers: drag, connect, activate.
tools.install: Start an n8n Cloud trial, or self-host with npm i -g n8n.
steps: Start n8n — the Cloud trial is fastest for beginners.
Build Webhook trigger → AI step → send/CRM action.
Activate, send a test event, then add the human-approval gate from L7.

tools.name: Node.js
tools.what: Runs JavaScript and dev servers on your machine.
tools.why: Required to run lesson servers, tools and build scripts locally.
tools.install: Install the LTS build from nodejs.org, then verify with node --version.
steps: Install the LTS build from nodejs.org for your OS.
Verify: node --version and npm --version both print numbers.
Run npm run dev in the lesson folder and open the printed URL.

tools.name: GitHub
tools.why: Backup for every project plus the portfolio employers actually open.
tools.install: Create an account at github.com, install git, set your name and email.
steps: Sign up at github.com and verify your email.
Set git config user.name and user.email in the terminal.
Push the lesson repo: init → add → commit → push (see L2M1L4).

tools.name: Git
tools.why: Undo mistakes and track exactly what changed, file by file.
tools.install: Install from git-scm.com (or Xcode tools / Git for Windows).
steps: Install git, then check git --version prints a number.
Practice status → add → commit → log in a scratch folder.
Learn undo: git restore for files, git revert for commits.

tools.name: Netlify
tools.what: Free static hosting with instant deploy previews.
tools.why: Publish Level 3 websites to a real link in minutes, free.
tools.install: Sign up at netlify.com, then drag-and-drop the build folder.
steps: Build the site (npm run build) and find the output folder.
Drag that folder onto Netlify Drop — or connect the GitHub repo.
Copy the live URL and test it on your phone.

tools.name: Expo
tools.what: Builds phone apps for iOS + Android.
tools.why: How this course itself ships to phones: one codebase, both stores.
tools.install: Install the CLI and scaffold with npx create-expo-app — see the docs.
steps: Install the CLI and scaffold the lesson app.
Run npx expo start and scan the QR with Expo Go.
Ship with EAS build → store tracks (see L10M2L5).

tools.name: Browser DevTools
tools.what: Inspect and debug any web page.
tools.why: See errors and fix layouts fast without guessing.
tools.install: Built into Chrome/Safari: press F12 (Mac: Cmd+Opt+I).
steps: Open your page and press F12 (Mac: Cmd+Opt+I).
Console tab: read the first red error top to bottom.
Elements tab: click the page, tweak CSS live, copy the fix.

tools.name: Terminal
tools.what: Command line to run servers and git.
tools.why: The essential developer skill this course teaches gently, step by step.
tools.install: Already built into Mac, Windows and Linux — no install needed.
steps: Open Terminal (Mac) or PowerShell/Terminal (Windows).
Practice: pwd → ls → cd into the lesson folder.
Run one safe command from the lesson, then echo hello.

P01.title: Personal Website
requirements: Your photo, bio and contact links included
setup: Install VS Code, open a folder named personal-site.
Scaffold 3 HTML pages sharing one stylesheet + one script.
Run a local server (npx serve .) and open the URL.
Create assets/ with one photo + favicon.
stages: Style hero, cards and footer mobile-first
Debug at phone width, then publish
prompts: GOAL: 3-page personal site (Home/About/Contact). CONTEXT: vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, one stylesheet. CONSTRAINTS: mobile-first, semantic tags. EXAMPLE: header/nav/main/footer per page.
GOAL: style system. CONTEXT: my unstyled pages. CONSTRAINTS: 2 fonts max, 3 colors. EXAMPLE: hero with headline + button.
GOAL: contact form. CONTEXT: no backend. CONSTRAINTS: validate email + message in-browser, success note. EXAMPLE: red hints, green confirm.
testing: Phone + desktop widths: no sideways scroll
Submit form empty (errors) then valid (success)
Every nav link lands on the right page + highlight
debugging: Blank page? DevTools Console → fix the first red error
Broken on phone? Toggle device toolbar, fix the breakpoint
deployment: Drag the folder to Netlify Drop
Open the live URL on your phone, keep the link

P02.title: Landing Page
setup: Sketch hero + 3 features on paper or one Figma phone frame.
Scaffold the page from your sketch with AI.
Serve locally, keep a phone-width window open while styling.
stages: Write copy: headline, subhead, CTA text
prompts: GOAL: landing page for [product]. CONTEXT: single file + styles. CONSTRAINTS: one CTA, mobile-first. EXAMPLE: hero, 3 features, signup, footer.
GOAL: sharper headline. CONTEXT: current draft. CONSTRAINTS: 5 options, plain words. EXAMPLE: one promise + one button.
GOAL: signup validation. CONTEXT: no backend. CONSTRAINTS: email check, inline errors, success without reload.
testing: Empty/invalid/valid signup → correct message each time
Phone + desktop visual pass, CTA visible without scroll
Images sized, no layout shift on load
debugging: Weak CTA? Read headline aloud — one promise, one button
Shift on load? Set image dimensions + preload the font
deployment: Publish via Netlify Drop or connected repo
Share live link + headline in Community for feedback
checklist: One clear CTA above the fold
Live URL + signup tested end to end

P03.title: CRUD Application
setup: Create crud-app, npm init -y, install minimal server deps.
Define the item shape {id, title, done} in one shared file.
Run API + client together, keep the Network tab open.
prompts: GOAL: REST API for items. CONTEXT: Node, JSON file store. CONSTRAINTS: GET/POST/PUT/DELETE, status codes. EXAMPLE: {id,title,done}.
GOAL: CRUD UI. CONTEXT: my API above. CONSTRAINTS: confirm before delete, optimistic list. EXAMPLE: add → appears instantly.
GOAL: resilient UI. CONTEXT: API can be down. CONSTRAINTS: friendly error card, retry button, skeleton rows.
testing: Happy path: add → see → edit → delete → gone
Stop the API: friendly error, never blank page
Refresh mid-list: everything still there
debugging: Network tab first: method, URL, status, body — in that order
Refresh wipes data? Save path disconnected — recheck write call
deployment: Host API + static client (one service or split)
Smoke-test all 4 operations on the live URL

P04.title: AI Chat Application
requirements: LLM via server route, system + user prompts
setup: Create LLM key, store ONLY server-side in .env.
Scaffold chat UI + POST /api/chat forwarding to the LLM.
Set caps: max tokens per reply + per day.
stages: Write system prompt: role, rules, refusals
Add caps, error fallback, cost log
prompts: GOAL: tutor system prompt. CONTEXT: beginners. CONSTRAINTS: short answers, one step at a time, refuse direct homework answers. EXAMPLE: hint, then check.
GOAL: better replies. CONTEXT: last 6 messages. CONSTRAINTS: stay in role, cite the step. EXAMPLE: good vs rambling reply.
GOAL: streaming + cap. CONTEXT: 200-token budget. CONSTRAINTS: render chunks, friendly “continued…” cutoff.
testing: 5 fixed questions → sane, on-role answers
Remove the key: fallback message, no crash
20-turn chat: coherent, cap enforced
debugging: Cost spike? Log prompt + tokens per reply, trim history
Garbled output? Enforce schema + retry once
deployment: Host web + server route, env vars in host dashboard
Watch day-one token usage against the cap

P05.title: Business Automation
requirements: Event trigger from a real source
setup: Create an n8n workflow with a manual test trigger.
Connect one source: form webhook or test event sender.
Enable dry-run: log actions instead of sending.
stages: Add approval gate, go live from dry-run
prompts: GOAL: classify lead. CONTEXT: raw message. CONSTRAINTS: intent + score 0-1 + route reply/escalate/ignore. EXAMPLE: scored sample.
GOAL: welcome reply. CONTEXT: my voice, new lead. CONSTRAINTS: 3 sentences, opt-out line. EXAMPLE: warm + short.
GOAL: approval summary. CONTEXT: run result. CONSTRAINTS: what, why, confidence in 4 lines.
testing: Dry-run: 10 events logged, zero sent
Approve → sent; reject → skipped + logged
Malformed event: skipped with reason, workflow stays green
debugging: Failed run? Open run history, compare node input vs expected shape
Misroutes? Add 2 examples to the prompt, re-run eval set
deployment: Activate n8n workflow or hosted route + scheduler
Go-live order: dry-run clean → approval tested → failure alerts on

P06.title: AI Customer Support System
requirements: FAQ bot grounded in your docs
Says “I don’t know” instead of inventing
setup: Write 10 FAQs as plain Q/A documents (the knowledge base).
Scaffold chat UI + /api/support with retrieval over FAQs.
Create the review queue for flagged answers.
prompts: GOAL: grounded answer. CONTEXT: retrieved docs below. CONSTRAINTS: answer ONLY from docs, else offer escalation. EXAMPLE: cited answer vs “I don’t know”.
GOAL: handoff summary. CONTEXT: full chat. CONSTRAINTS: issue, tried steps, sentiment in 5 lines.
GOAL: quality flag. CONTEXT: bot answer + docs. CONSTRAINTS: correct/partial/wrong + missing doc.
testing: 15 FAQ questions → grounded + correct; 5 off-topic → graceful “don’t know”
Escalation always carries transcript + summary
Spot-check 20 answers against docs, zero inventions
debugging: Wrong answer? Check WHICH doc retrieved — fix the doc first
Hallucinations? Lower temperature, stricter “docs-only”, cite sources
deployment: Host web + API; KB editable without redeploy
Put the weekly review on your calendar

P07.title: AI Agent
setup: Define the goal + 2 tools (search, save) with JSON schemas.
Write the allowlist: exactly what the agent may call/send.
Seed one run log to observe plan → act → verify.
